To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the cross-sectional analyses showed a strong association between socio-demographics, motivational variables and smoking behaviour, and 2) the longitudinal analyses revealed that the change of status from nonsmoking to regular smoking after one year was explained by low baseline self-efficacy, having more smoking peers, and playing truant.
The cross-sectional analysis of the data revealed that 76% of the variance of smoking onset was explained by socio-demographic and motivational variables.

the predictors of smoking onset are: having more smoking friends, having low self-efficacies in refraining from cigarettes in different situations, playing truant from high school and having a brother (a protective factor).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and assessment of factors which are associated with smoking onset.
the prediction of smoking initiation among adolescents.
the development of a model of smoking behaviour among adolescents.

the study showed that there is a need for more research in Romania to identify the factors which predict adolescent smoking behaviour and that the results suggest that smoking cessation programmes in Romania should be developed and strengthened.

the study has identified some predictors for smoking onset in a Romanian sample, but that there is a lack of studies that would allow for a comparison with other countries.
